      THE COMBINATION IS THE SIGNAL

      Familiar enough to recognise?

      A fingerprint combines browser and rendering characteristics. It can help group visits. It does not prove who you are, and it may change or be shared by many devices.

      ◎

      A signature, not a secret identity

      These locally computed hashes demonstrate how several readings can be combined. We do not measure population uniqueness, store a tracking identifier, or compare your browser with other visitors.

      Browser-reported inputsMay be coarsened or spoofedLocal computation
      ⓘ

      WebGL extensions describe graphics capabilities. They are unrelated to installed browser extensions. A canvas hash may be shared by many systems or modified by privacy protections.

      UNDERSTAND WHAT STAYS HIDDEN

      Powerful. Not all-seeing.

      A page observes its own environment and interactions. Some events can suggest what happened; they cannot reveal the whole story.

      THE OBSERVATORY FIELD GUIDE

      Learn the signals.

      Plain-language explanations, linked to the web platform documentation.

      How this demo treats your data

      Readings live in page memory. There are no analytics services, external fonts, advertising pixels, accounts, or session databases. The server handles ordinary request metadata and displays a limited subset back to you. The demo endpoint writes no logs or database records; the hosting provider may keep ordinary access logs. Permission demos read only what their card describes. Export downloads a report to your device when you click it. Reloading or ending a session clears its in-memory data; your browser may retain permission grants.

      “No new permissions” does not mean “no collection”, and this demonstration is a broad inventory, not a promise to cover every browser feature, tracking method, or malicious website.
